column1: # Primer set for amphid - OPTIONAL input (--primers)
# A separate file from the assay config on purpose: primers travel with the
# PANEL, not with the construct. Change the targets and the primers may
# change too, while the Nextera overhangs, the control tag and the index
# design stay put.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR
#   One thing only: validating reference EXTENT. Primers are not needed to
#   assign a locus (competitive mapping gives that) nor to set length windows
#   (reference length gives those). But they are the only way to check that
#   every reference entry spans exactly primer-to-primer.
#   That matters because an entry carrying extra sequence outside its primer
#   sites offers more alignable bases than its competitors, biasing
#   assignment toward it for reasons unrelated to what is actually present -
#   and it hides inside genuine biological length variation, where no
#   length-based check can find it.
#   Pre-flight reports, per entry, which primer pair was found and how many
#   bases lie outside them. Uniform is what matters: a panel where every
#   entry carries the same flank is coherent; one where some do and some do
#   not is not.
# In phase 2 the same file supplies the mask coordinates for variant calling,
# since primer-derived bases are synthetic rather than sample-derived.
# COLUMNS
#   name        free text
#   direction   fwd | rev
#   sequence    as ordered, 5'->3'. Reverse primers are given as ordered;
#               the pipeline reverse-complements them to find the 3' site.
